statement: For the ordinary rooted d-ary one-frog model, d>=2, E[N_root including time zero] = d/(d-1)(1+sum_{n>=1}p_n), where p_n is the ever-activation probability of a fixed depth-n vertex. Summability gives transience; infinite expectation alone gives no recurrence conclusion.
assumptions: one active root frog and one sleeper per non-root vertex
independent simple random walks on the infinite rooted d-ary tree
integer d>=2

assumptions: One sleeping resident per vertex
Ordinary parent step p=1/4
At most K awakening-enabled arrivals per child edge
All waking suppressed during each overflow excursion; motion retained
Causal rule never queries a sleeping resident walk

No other active frogs

statement: For the ordinary one-frog d-ary model, if a legitimate finite-origin lower family R_H retains only original paths, counts each first root absorption once and wakes residents only through height H below the first entered child, then P(full root returns infinite)>=d limsup E[R_H]/H. Positive linear limsup gives ordinary recurrence by HJJ zero-one law.
assumptions: Integer d>=2; ordinary parent probability 1/(d+1)
One incoming initial root frog plus original residents at levels0..H
No cloned origins; ordinary retained paths; one first-hit absorption per frog
Lower first-hit counts contained in full ordinary activity
sources: https://arxiv.org/abs/1404.6238 Theorem4 for ordinary zero-one law

audits.reason: PASS as numerical evidence on sha256 cc2958bfdd95077c. The table was recomputed from the 24 root records in C29_STAGE_v2.json (sha 0cb66059, every root absolute level 0, M=4000, replicates 0-2 for each of the 8 cells): every mean R1, between-run SD, PGF(1/2) mean and SD matches to the printed digits. Exact envelopes checked by hand against C30 v1: mu_H = 1/3 + (H+1)/3 = (H+2)/3. On E (the incoming seed and the resident at u both step inward, prob 1/16) both hit o at once, nothing enters the subtree, R_H = 2. The level n>=1 indicators are independent of E with total mean H/3, so E R_H <= mu_H - (1/16)(2+H/3) + 2/16 = (H+2)/3 - H/48, which is 122/3 at H=128, above the observed 34.898. At p=6/25, beta = p/(1-p) = 6/19 and 3beta = 18/19, so E C_H < beta + beta/(1-3beta) = 120/19. The floor of 1/4 for any genuine lower family's threshold is correct (3beta<1 gives finite expected hits). Scope stated correctly: no exact-law mean growth and no threshold are claimed; C29 v1's PASS is not transferred; the unfinished M=16000 campaign is excluded. Not re-run: the simulator itself.

statement: For any d>=2, 0<p<1/2 and deterministic finite positive absolute-depth entry budgets K_j, the retained-motion/suppressed-overflow serial lower model has the exact finite-height law mu_H=L_KH, mu_j=T_(Kj,Kj+1)(mu_j+1). The unequal-cap operators are finite and monotone in cumulative child maps, the fixed-profile horizon laws are monotone, and at ordinary p=1/(d+1) their one-seed responses satisfy the original-path finite-origin lower coupling required by C30.
assumptions: Integer d>=2; 0<p<1/2; independent ordinary directions
One original resident per vertex, persistent counters and joint serial input responses
Deterministic absolute-depth finite positive budgets, fixed across horizons
Overflow suppresses ALL waking until return and consumes no enabled counters or departure stack
Only original resident origins through horizon H; each first root hit counted once
The full-model comparison and C30 application here use ordinary p=1/(d+1)

statement: For k deterministic enabled inputs and one resident in C31, enabled entries N_c into a specified child of budget B admit N_c>=min(B,S), S~Bin(k+1,r), r=q/(1-(d-1)q beta). On ordinary T3 r=3/10. Forced-query no-child-entry errors are summable for logarithmic profiles 4^K>=(j+2)^alpha with alpha=4 or 8; this does not supply the inputs or prove recurrence.
assumptions: C31 finite-horizon serial retained-path model, d>=2 and 0<p<1/2
k is prescribed deterministically in a fresh query; each input begins enabled; one resident only
B>=1; cumulative counters persist; ordinary suppressed motion retained

statement: Finite rooted prefix-block episodes that clone only nonancestral residents on upward entry dominate the ordinary frog model. For independent stopped personal ranges, closure masses obey g_s(S) prod(v in S)g_v(S)=sum(T subset S) q_T prod(v in S minus T)g_v(S), giving exact rational site offspring means. A positive-potential contraction checked also at the exceptional global-root block implies finite expected root visits. No T4 certificate is asserted.
assumptions: Ordinary rooted d-ary tree, d>=2, one sleeping frog away from the root, finitely many initial root frogs
Finite rooted prefix-closed block and all ordinary motion retained
Only the ancestral path of an upward entry is guaranteed warm; other permitted residents wake once per episode
Potential criterion must cover every attachment context and returning entry into the global-root block
gap: Pathwise upper coupling and finite formulas await independent review. No ordinary T4 contraction or summable activation upper bound has been established. Novelty unassessed.

statement: For C33 copied block episodes, downward-rounded lower iterations x_next=A_T+sum B_T,e*x*y_e and y_c_next=A_c+sum B_c,e*x*y_e witness infinite expected upper-process root visits whenever x_n*min_c sum_e D_c,e>=1. Ordinary T4 five-site star and nine-site one-expanded-child blocks both meet this criterion at n=4. Thus these copied upper comparisons cannot prove finite-mean transience by C33 potentials. No conclusion about the ordinary frog model is asserted.
assumptions: Precisely the C33 independent copied-block law with all ordinary walks and unbounded entries
Only the ancestral path is guaranteed warm on upward entry; other allowed residents wake once per fresh episode
Global root degree d and bulk degree d+1
Positive probability of reaching a returning root episode; finite set of entry categories
